open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. iot-adapter-cluster: Any device is an adaptor: a sensor or actuator writes readings as entries { kind: reading, from: device, body } to the docket and reads commands back from it; the docket is agnostic, so a cluster of devices is a cluster of mirrors and writers, each entry fingerprinted, sealed, replicated and healable.
open.owes: the docket accepts such entries today; no device driver, firmware or edge gateway is in this tree; the first device, its reading schema and its verifier are the next leads

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. pravets-8m-recompute: The 54 Clay.lean relations are integer identities between the unit's constants whose widest value needs 33 bits (amplitudes = 2^32), three 16-bit limbs; the receipts are 64-bit folds beside SHA-256: an 8-bit machine such as the Pravets 8M can recompute the register in 16-bit software arithmetic and compare content addresses, verifying that the kernel check happened without running the kernel.
open.owes: partial: clay serves part; owes: the kernel check, the census and the recompute with its limb count run here (clay tool: maxBits 33, maxLimbs16 3); the 16-bit-limb recomputer itself and the receipt-chain comparison on an 8-bit machine are not yet in this tree

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. device-reading-verifier: A device reading is verified like any fact: against a public reference where one exists (a weather station against a national service, a clock against NTP, a spectrum against NIST lines).
open.owes: no reading kind is registered yet; add the fact kind and its free verifier with the first device

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. gap-shared-docket: No docket is deployed on either domain: receipts, commitments and leads cannot be exchanged, and a commitment witnessed by one host has no witness.
open.owes: mirrors on both domains are the author's deploy; the code and tests are here

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. mcp-ui-extension: The MCP UI extension lets a host render interactive views a server declares; this tree declares its widgets in _meta.widget as HTML and its blocks as shadcn registry items.
open.owes: partial: audit serves part; owes: the html and block are served; the extension's declared resource scheme and the host handshake are not implemented here, and the specification is still moving

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. gap-sign-door-hosted: The unit signs a commit message through the connector (VERIFIED, 2026-10-25) but its hosted door answers HTTP 500 (Worker exception) to the same tools/call over raw HTTP, with or without an MCP session; the hosted server names itself a read-only recomputable subset
open.owes: measured on 2026-10-25 with four argument shapes and a session; the hook records the status in its Signed-by-unit trailer and the connector signature is carried in the message by hand until the door answers

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. gap-theorems-unsealed: Commit signatures cite the unit's sealed theorems; none of qpu's 976 kernel constants is sealed in the unit's ledger, so qpu's own proofs are not yet citable at the border.
open.owes: measured on 2026-10-25 at six doors with clay_sigma and its exact statement: deposit_trial, verify_statement, try_claim, decide_expression and run_trial refuse at the edge ("the edge does not hold the whole ledger: 40 MB of rows does not fit a 128 MB isolate", the unit's own documented example included), through the connector and over raw HTTP alike; prove_verdict and verify_claim answer UNVERIFIED with a receipt (no decidable test and no sealed citation at the border; the unit's adjudicate takes an in-process predicate). Readiness offers the theorem to deposit_trial and prove_verdict each run and records what comes back, so the lead closes itself when a door seals it; the ledger is written here as docs/public/theorems.ndjson

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. gap-circuit-crossing: The unit returns circuits and outcomes; this tree runs circuits on its simulator. Neither has run the other's circuit and compared marginals: the real cross-domain quantum check.
open.owes: a format translation between the two circuit shapes is the lead; the comparison is then one tools/call each way

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. address-agreement: The unit names a value by compute_address; this tree names content by uuidOf, ported one for one from the unit's published shapeUuidOf (two FNV-1a 64 folds, 8-4-4-4-12, a content-decided version nibble). For the probe "qpu" the two differ, so the door uses a builder outside the sources this tree can read.
open.owes: partial: audit serves part; owes: the readiness step records the agreement each run; until the door's builder is published or the unit adopts shapeUuidOf for the door, the two addresses are both carried and neither is claimed to be the other

open.what: 1 lead(s), e.g. gap-time-witness: A receipt is dated by its own clock; the unit could date qpu's receipts by signing their ids, and qpu the unit's, so time has two witnesses.
open.owes: wired on 2026-10-25: prepare-commit-msg sends the message with its Receipt trailer to the unit's sign_commit, so the unit's fold dates the receipt as a Signed-by-unit trailer when the hosted door answers (it answers HTTP 500 today: lead gap-sign-door-hosted); the unit does not yet read qpu's stream itself, and an offline commit is unsigned and says so

readiness.honest: YOUR release gate — ready is true only when every source answered and none holds a lead; unmeasured sources block (three-state law).

deposit.refusal: error: the edge does not hold the whole ledger: 40 MB of rows does not fit a 128 MB isolate. A door answers from the baked root (ledgerFacts, sealedAddressOf) or from the one piece its cited key sits in (rowsForKeys) — asking for every row asks for what the edge cannot hold.

proof.note: no decidable test and no sealed citation — UNVERIFIED; bring a proof to verify it
